newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - July 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - July 21.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Superannuation funds managers have achieved their best result since the 1987 stockmarket collapse, but warn the 1997-98 year will be more difficult. Tyndall Funds Management achieved a 51 per cent return on its Australian share fund, while BNP achieved 398 per cent, Integrated Equity achieved 36.3 per cent, Mercantile Mutual achieved 36.1 per cent, and First State achieved 35.4 per cent. Page 1.

Australia's largest exporter of manufactured goods, Holden's Motor Overseas Corporation Ltd suffered from lower demand and the strains of its investment program last year to record a 64 per cent slump in profits to A$14.5 million. HMOC director Peter Thoms said yesterday the earnings outlook for 1997 was better. Page 19.

Dozens of companies have expressed interest in the New South Wales TAB's poker machine jackpots licence, and the organisation is also considering whether to completely contract out that part of its business. The TAB has asked interested parties to bid forparts or all of the poker machine jackpot system. Page 19.

The first joint board meeting of Qantas and its 25 percent shareholder British Airways last week instructed the companies' management to investigate possible future co-operation between the two services, including joint use of aircraft, joint purchasing, shared air terminals, and the possible development of new in-flight entertainment systems.
Page 21.

A spokeswoman for Optus said yesterday Optus Communications was not the mystery buyer of around four per cent of Australis Media's shares. The spokeswoman said Optus would be concerned if a merger, currently being discussed between Australis and rival pay-TV group Foxtel, resulted in anti-competitive behaviour. Page 23.

The Seven Network announced on Friday it would undertake a A$325 million capital raising to lengthen its debt maturity and improve its debt-to-equity ratio to 48 percent, back from 65 percent in December. The A$75 million share placement was completed o Friday, with the remainder to be made up of a A$250 million senior note placement. Page 23.
THE AUSTRALIAN

Small Business Minister Peter Reith said yesterday he may argue for a small business representative to be appointed to the Reserve Bank board following the upcoming retirements of Solomon Lew and Janet Holmes a Court. Reith said the Federal Government had done a lot for small business but still had to do more. Page 17.

The Taxation Institute of Australia, the Australian Society of CPAs and the Institute of Chartered Accountants have jointly condemned the National Tax and Accountants Association's opposition to proposed new standards for tax agents. The NTAA claims the sandards will expose tax agents to greater penalties and so require them to audit their clients, possibly doubling the cost of preparing a tax return. Page 17.

Insurance company FAI has claimed MMI abused the disclosure rules of the Australian Stock Exchange in its efforts to beat down the agreed price of A$50 million for FAI's New Zealand operations. FAI chief executive Rodney Adler said MMI's public announcemet of the sale means the asset will always be considered for sale, regardless of what the company says. Page 19.

A subsidiary of Acclaim Exploration NL, Acclaim NL, has lodged a prospectus to raise funds for a uranium exploration program in Western Australia. It is the first uranium explorer to do so since the Federal Government scrapped the three-mines uranium polcy. Acclaim NL has 15 potential projects, and aims to raise A$5 million for its program. Page 19.

Australian Wheat Board treasury operations head Michael Doyle has warned the AWB its long term credit rating could be downgraded following full commercialisation in 1999. Doyle also said interest on the AWB's A$3 billion annual borrowings could rise, but e would be surprised if the board's short-term credit rating was downgraded. Page 19.

Shareholders in Budget housing and apartment developer Devine have approved an increase in the company's capital which would help fund a push into the Sydney and Melbourne residential markets. Devine managing director David Devine said the timing was righ for the interstate move, following the acquisition of Pioneer Homes' contract housing division. Page 19.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Evidence of a weak economy in many sectors indicates the possibility of another interest rate cut by the Reserve Bank, with the Consumer Price Index expected to fall below one per cent and the underlying inflation rate expected below two per cent for the year to June, when the figures are released this week. Page 37.

Australian Chamber of Manufactures chief executive Allan Handberg expressed concern last night that Ford's employee pay deal of 15.75 per cent over three years might put pressure on other employers. The major car makers' settlements are traditionally usedas a benchmark for the manufacturing industry when negotiating wage deals. Page 37.

Howard Smith is seeking to defend against the entry of Victorian-based Bunnings into the New South Wales hardware market by buying BBC Hardwarehouse stores from Burns, Philp and Company for up to A$60 million. Bunnings managing director Warren Murphy said the group was aiming for 20 sites in New South Wales and Queensland by 2000. Page 39.

The A$2.2 billion sale of ICI plc's stake in ICI Australia marks the independence of the Australian company from its British parent after 69 years, although some commercial agreements between the two companies will not expire for some time. Page 37.

Small Business and Workplace Relations Minister Peter Reith expects industrial relations to be a key issue at the next election and has confirmed plans for further reforms, with the Federal Government ready to come down on big businesses which exploit ther power when dealing with smaller businesses. Page 39.

The ANZ Bank says houses have been the safest and most profitable form of investment over the past decade, outperforming the sharemarket by 50 per cent, but warns that over the short to medium term the sharemarket has outperformed residential property. Pae 41.
THE AGE

Australian Chamber of Manufactures chief executive Allan Handberg last night said Ford's 15.75 per cent pay deal over three years could make it difficult for smaller companies for whom the big car maker's wage deals have served as a benchmark. The Ford del appears to be well above the Reserve Bank's desired 4.5 per cent per year ceiling. Page B1.

The recovery of gold prices continued over the weekend, almost to the level before the Reserve Bank announced its two-thirds sale of its gold holdings. Analysts said the increasing price was due to demand from jewellers and manufacturers. Demand for Austrlian-listed gold stocks is expected to dampen the impact of a late fall in New York on Friday. Page B1.

Deloitte Touche Tohmatsu accountants and Corrs Chambers Westgarth lawyers have been ordered by the Supreme Court to pay more than A$1.8 million in damages for misleading conduct and negligence in a due diligence inquiry relating to the failed spa maker UF Group. Page B2.

Howard Smith is preparing for the imminent arrival of Bunnings into the New South Wales hardware market by spending up to $A60 million on key suburban Sydney BBC Hardwarehouse stores owned by Burns Philp. The move will improve earnings for Howard Smith by removing leasing costs and assist Burns Philp in reducing borrowings. Page B3.

The Australian Society of Certified Practising Accountants says the results of the latest CPA quarterly Small Business Health Index - a survey of 450 small companies in Sydney, Melbourne and Brisbane - highlights the severe tax compliance burden on small usiness, which could cost them up to $A7 billion each year. Page B3.

Lucky Buys Reward director Bruno Campisi said his new customer loyalty scheme aimed at small business was different to the big business loyalty marketing criticised as ineffectual in recent studies. The research by BIS Shrapnel found schemes such as Fly Bys, Global Rewards and Frequent Flyer did not induce brand or business loyalty. Page B3.
-- Reuters Sydney newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
